topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the core learning outcomes for the final lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain standard therapeutic modalities that physically remove or broadly damage rapidly dividing cells alongside their associated clinical limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively exploit cancer cell weaknesses, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies, oncogene addiction, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the identification of driver oncogenes, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and the biological mechanisms of acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and targeted drug delivery
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the application of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively bind tumor-associated surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell modulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for anti-tumor immunity and the therapeutic reactivation or engineering of T cells against cancer.

topics.label: Overall challenges, clinical progress, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the overarching challenges of tumor heterogeneity, historical survival trends, and future clinical perspectives in cancer treatment.
